newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila T-bill market focuses on short-term bills.
newsitem.headline: Manila T-bill market focuses on short-term bills.

text.p: Philippine banks snapped up short-term cash management bills on Wednesday to satisfy clients' requirements, traders said.
"The demand is on the 35-day and 42-day bills because the rates are higher compared to the other tenors," one trader said.
At the auction on Tuesday, the average rate on the 35-day bill rose to 17.527 percent from 15.617 percent last week; and the rate on the 42-day bill increased to 17.679 percent from 15.770 percent.
Banks, however, continued to shy away from the long-term bills because of the uncertainty in the currency market.
"No one's taking the six-month and one-year bills," the trader said.

The average interbank call loan rate dipped to 20.46875 percent from 20.9375 percent. In line with the easing in the money market, the central bank on Wednesday dropped its overnight lending rate to 25 percent from 26 percent.
On Monday, it had raised the overnight lending rate by four percentage points in anticipation of a tigthening in liquidity with the additional reserves imposed on banks.
Market volume was almost steady at 20.20 billion pesos from the previous day's 20.21 billion.
Out of the 52 participating financial institutions, 33 were lenders.
